key_insight: Bayesian inference combined with photoluminescence imaging and drift-diffusion modeling can localize where perovskite solar cells degrade and distinguish whether the damage comes from the bulk or from a transport-layer interface.
engineering_relevance: This enables targeted reliability improvements by identifying the specific spatial regions and interfaces that most strongly drive performance loss, and by showing that amino-silane passivation can suppress those failure modes.
method: Photoluminescence imaging of fully fabricated perovskite solar cells
Drift-diffusion simulations linked to Bayesian inference to infer recombination-parameter maps
Time-resolved tracking of those maps during accelerated aging at 70 °C under full-spectrum sunlight
evidence_signal: The abstract reports spatially non-uniform inferred parameter maps during aging, with the strongest degradation localized to perovskite/transport-layer interfaces and reduced by amino-silane passivation.
watch_item: The inferred maps depend on the accuracy of the drift-diffusion model and imaging assumptions, so model mismatch could bias the attribution of degradation pathways.
paper_title: Disentangling the origin of degradation in perovskite solar cells via optical imaging and Bayesian inference
